Ambient Orchestration — class diagram Class diagram showing AmbientOrchestratorAgent and its relationships to DatabaseSessionService, FlightAgent, CalendarAgent, NotificationComposer, the three committee stubs, and the MCP tool functions.
AmbientOrchestratorAgent
flight_number: str meeting_id: str flight_airlinecode: str flight_date: date scheduled_arrival: datetime user_email: str session_id: str initial_state: dict
+ start() ~ _loop() async ~ _sensing_cycle() async ~ _fetch_flight_status() async ~ _compute_delay_minutes() ~ _send_email() async ~ _sync(changes) async
DatabaseSessionService
db_url: str (sqlite+aiosqlite)
+ get_session() + create_session() + append_event(state_delta) → ADK event journal
FlightAgent ADK root_agent
runner: InMemoryRunner
run_async(prompt) → FlightStatusRealtime
FlightStatusRealtime Pydantic model
Departure_Airport: str Arrival_Airport: str Departure_Time: datetime Arrival_Time: datetime Status: str
NotificationComposer DSPy module
load(path: str) __call__(scenario: dict) → prediction.notification
CalendarAgent
execute(prompt: str) reschedule + update description → run via run_in_executor
Committee agents (stubs)
_call_time_agent() → {p_arrive_by_deadline: 0.78}
_call_risk_agent() → {delay_multiplier: 1.25}
_call_impact_agent() → {meeting_weight: 0.85}
MCP tools (module-level)
get_weather(lat, lon) → dict estimate_route(origin, dest) → dict get_calendar(meeting_id) → dict from backend.src.mcp.fastmcp_server imported at module level
